title: Audio: kill or cut the 2s fake lead-in on phone speak
Find the 2s lead-in and the all-at-once workaround in the speak path
Measure what Bluetooth actually needs, from logcat on the real Pixel
Cut or remove the lead-in; keep the single-clip behaviour intact
Prove on PaseoDF: logcat timings plus Des's ear test

stage: Locating the lead-in

note: RESULT: both found. 2s lead-in = packages/server/src/server/agent/tts-manager.ts:46 leadInSilence(), LEAD_IN_SILENCE_SECONDS=2, digital silence prepended to chunk 0 only (so paid once per report). All-at-once workaround = packages/app/src/audio/group-playback.ts buildAudioPlaybackSource(), which decodes every chunk and concatenates into one buffer. ROOT CAUSE of the car quality, beyond the lead-in: speak is played through @getpaseo/expo-two-way-audio, a duplex voice engine — native SAMPLE_RATE=16000, AudioTrack USAGE_VOICE_COMMUNICATION + CONTENT_TYPE_SPEECH, audioManager.mode=MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION — and pcm/index.ts:102 resamples the 24 kHz TTS down to 16 kHz first. MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION with a car connected routes over HFP/SCO (~8 kHz narrowband), not A2DP. Same cause explains the 2s padding (slow SCO setup), o4/o6 (session and focus held, music never resumes) and why streaming chunks was awkward.

text: Root cause found: speak plays on the voice-communication engine (16 kHz, MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION) so the car gets narrowband SCO instead of A2DP
